theory.intro: The projectile model gives $\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=-g\underset{\sim}{j}$, with $g$ positive and up positive. Integrating once and using the initial velocity gives $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$. Integrating again and using the initial position gives $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.
facts: Each integration introduces a **constant of integration** in each component, found from the initial conditions.
The horizontal acceleration is zero, so $\dot{x}=V\cos\alpha$ stays the same for the whole flight.
The vertical velocity is $\dot{y}=-gt+V\sin\alpha$, dropping by $g$ every second.
Integrating again from the origin gives $x=Vt\cos\alpha$ and $y=-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}+Vt\sin\alpha$.
A launch from height $h$ replaces $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$ with $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=h\underset{\sim}{j}$, which adds $h$ to $y$.
You are expected to show the constants being found, since quoting the six equations earns no marks.
steps: Write the acceleration in vector form
Use the initial velocity to find the constants
Use the initial position to find the constants

foundation.question_text:
A projectile is fired from the origin at $28\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
Integrating $\ddot{y}=-10$ gives $\dot{y}=-10t+C$.
Find $C$.

A ball is thrown from the origin at $24\text{ m/s}$ at $60^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
By integrating, find $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$ in exact form.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Write the acceleration in vector form**
$\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=0\underset{\sim}{i}-10\underset{\sim}{j}$
2. **Integrate to find the velocity**
$\underset{\sim}{v}=C_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+(-10t+C_{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$
3. **Use the initial velocity to find the constants**
$\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=24\cos 60^{\circ}\,\underset{\sim}{i}+24\sin 60^{\circ}\,\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=12\underset{\sim}{i}+12\sqrt{3}\underset{\sim}{j}$
$C_{1}=12$ and $C_{2}=12\sqrt{3}$
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=12\underset{\sim}{i}+(12\sqrt{3}-10t)\underset{\sim}{j}$

foundation.question_text:
A projectile launched from the origin has $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=9\underset{\sim}{i}+(20-10t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres per second.
Find $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.
foundation.solution_text:
4. **Integrate to find the position**
$\underset{\sim}{r}=(9t+C_{3})\underset{\sim}{i}+(20t-5t^{2}+C_{4})\underset{\sim}{j}$
5. **Use the initial position to find the constants**
$\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$
$C_{3}=0$ and $C_{4}=0$
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=9t\underset{\sim}{i}+(20t-5t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$

foundation.question_text:
A stone is thrown from the origin at $15\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ **below** the horizontal.
Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
Find $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$ in exact form.

A ball is projected from the origin at $45\text{ m/s}$ at $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)$ above the horizontal.
Integrating $\ddot{x}=0$ gives $\dot{x}=C$.
Find $C$.

A ball is thrown from the origin at $16\text{ m/s}$ at $60^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
Derive the six equations of motion, giving exact values.

development.question_text:
A ball is thrown from a platform $12\text{ m}$ above the ground with speed $25\text{ m/s}$ at $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)$ above the horizontal.
Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and measure $y$ from the ground.
Find $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.

A student derives the motion of a projectile launched from the origin at $V\text{ m/s}$ at angle $\alpha$, taking $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
Line 1: $\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=-10\underset{\sim}{i}-10\underset{\sim}{j}$
Line 2: $\underset{\sim}{v}=(-10t+C_{1})\underset{\sim}{i}+(-10t+C_{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$
Line 3: $C_{1}=V\cos\alpha$ and $C_{2}=V\sin\alpha$
Identify the first incorrect line and correct it.
development.solution_text:
Line 1 is the first incorrect line.
There is no horizontal force, so $\ddot{x}=0$.
$\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=-10\underset{\sim}{j}$

development.question_text:
A projectile launched from a roof $8\text{ m}$ above the ground has $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=14\underset{\sim}{i}+(21-9.8t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres per second, with $y$ measured from the ground.
A student integrates and writes $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=14t\underset{\sim}{i}+(21t-4.9t^{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$.
Identify the error and correct it.
development.solution_text:
The student used $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$, but the launch is $8\text{ m}$ above the ground.
$\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=8\underset{\sim}{j}$, so $C_{4}=8$.
$\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=14t\underset{\sim}{i}+(21t-4.9t^{2}+8)\underset{\sim}{j}$

development.question_text:
A shot is projected from the origin at $26\text{ m/s}$ at $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{12}\right)$ above the horizontal.
Take $g=9.8\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
Derive $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)$ and $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.

A particle is projected from the origin with initial velocity $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=11\underset{\sim}{i}+18\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres per second.
Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
Find $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)$.

A ball leaves a bat $1.2\text{ m}$ above the ground at $30\text{ m/s}$ at $40^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
Take $g=9.8\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and measure $y$ from the ground.
Integrating $\dot{y}=-9.8t+30\sin 40^{\circ}$ gives $y=-4.9t^{2}+30t\sin 40^{\circ}+C$.
Find $C$.

mastery.question_text:
A projectile is launched from the origin with speed $V$ at angle $\alpha$ above the horizontal, with $\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=-g\underset{\sim}{j}$.
By integrating twice, show that $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=Vt\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+\left(Vt\sin\alpha-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$.
mastery.solution_text:
2. **Integrate to find the velocity**
$\underset{\sim}{v}=C_{1}\underset{\sim}{i}+(-gt+C_{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$
3. **Use the initial velocity to find the constants**
$\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=V\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+V\sin\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{j}$
$C_{1}=V\cos\alpha$ and $C_{2}=V\sin\alpha$
$\underset{\sim}{v}=V\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(V\sin\alpha-gt)\underset{\sim}{j}$
4. **Integrate to find the position**
$\underset{\sim}{r}=(Vt\cos\alpha+C_{3})\underset{\sim}{i}+\left(Vt\sin\alpha-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}+C_{4}\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$
5. **Use the initial position to find the constants**
$\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$, so $C_{3}=0$ and $C_{4}=0$
$\underset{\sim}{r}=Vt\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+\left(Vt\sin\alpha-\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}\right)\underset{\sim}{j}$

mastery.question_text:
A projectile launched from a tower has $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=18t\underset{\sim}{i}+(24t-5t^{2}+30)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, with $y$ measured from the ground.
Find the value of $g$ being used, the height of the tower, and the launch speed and angle to 1 d.p.
mastery.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=18\underset{\sim}{i}+(24-10t)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=-10\underset{\sim}{j}$
$g=10$
$\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=30\underset{\sim}{j}$, so the tower is $30\text{ m}$ high.
$V=\sqrt{18^{2}+24^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{900}$
$=30$
$\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{24}{18}\right)$
$\approx 53.1^{\circ}$
The launch was at $30\text{ m/s}$, $53.1^{\circ}$ above the horizontal, from a tower $30\text{ m}$ high, with $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$.

mastery.question_text:
A student derives the motion of a ball launched from the origin at $V\text{ m/s}$ at angle $\alpha$, with $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
Line 1: $\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=-10\underset{\sim}{j}$
Line 2: $\underset{\sim}{v}=V\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(-10t+V\sin\alpha)\underset{\sim}{j}$
Line 3: $\underset{\sim}{r}=Vt\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(-10t^{2}+Vt\sin\alpha)\underset{\sim}{j}$
Identify the first incorrect line, explain the error, and give the correct equation.
mastery.solution_text:
Line 3 is the first incorrect line.
$\int -10t\,dt=-5t^{2}$, not $-10t^{2}$; the power rule halves the coefficient.
$\underset{\sim}{r}=Vt\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+(-5t^{2}+Vt\sin\alpha)\underset{\sim}{j}$
